entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-5q66-v53q-pm35: Keycloak vulnerable to Plaintext Storage of User Password
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to Plaintext Storage of User Password

Aliases: CVE-2023-4918

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-core — fixed in 22.0.3

A flaw was discovered in Keycloak Core package. When a user registers itself through registration flow, the "password" and "password-confirm" field from the form will occur as regular attributes in the users attributes. The password is also created, but the user attributes must not be there. This way, any entities (all users and clients with proper rights/roles) are able to retrieve the users passwords in clear-text. ### Impact Passwords for self-registered users are stored as cleartext attributes associated with the user. ### Mitigation Disable self-registration for users in all realms until patched.

  • https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/security/advisories/GHSA-5q66-v53q-pm35

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-5rxp-2rhr-qwqv: Keycloak has session fixation in Elytron SAML adapters
entry.content:
Keycloak has session fixation in Elytron SAML adapters

Aliases: CVE-2024-7341, GHSA-j76j-rqwj-jmvv

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 22.0.12
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 24.0.7
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 25.0.5

A session fixation issue was discovered in the SAML adapters provided by Keycloak. The session ID and JSESSIONID cookie are not changed at login time, even when the turnOffChangeSessionIdOnLogin option is configured. This flaw allows an attacker who hijacks the current session before authentication to trigger session fixation.

The tracer allocates a hash-map entry for each pair on every request, causing unbounded CPU and memory consumption and enabling a remote Denial of Service against any HTTP service that has the baggage propagation style enabled. The baggage propagation style is enabled by default in mos…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-jhq6-gfmj-v8fx: Logback vulnerable to Object Injection through HardenedObjectInputStream modules
entry.content:
Logback vulnerable to Object Injection through HardenedObjectInputStream modules

Aliases: CVE-2026-10532

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N/E:P/RE:M/U:Green

Affected:

  • ch.qos.logback:logback-core — fixed in 1.5.34

Deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in QOS.CH Sarl logback logback-core (HardenedObjectInputStream (logback-core) modules) allows Object Injection, albeit heavily restricted. More precisely, an attacker able to influence serialized data sent to SimpleSocketServer or SimpleSSLSocketServer can instantiate Proxy objects. Although deserialization is heavily restricted by HardenedObjectInputStream and no practical way to achieve remote code execution or significant privilege escalation has been identified, this issue constitutes a bypass of the intended security restrictions. This issue affects logback: through 1.5.33 inclusive.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-22rm-wp4x-v5cx: Keycloak Server-Side Request Forgery via OIDC token endpoint manipulation
entry.content:
Keycloak Server-Side Request Forgery via OIDC token endpoint manipulation

Aliases: CVE-2026-4874

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.3
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.4.13

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated attacker can perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) by manipulating the `client_session_host` parameter during refresh token requests. This occurs when a Keycloak client is configured to use the `backchannel.logout.url` with the `application.session.host` placeholder. Successful exploitation allows the attacker to make HTTP requests from the Keycloak server’s network context, potentially probing internal networks or internal APIs, leading to information disclosure.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-5v8v-xvjv-57x7: Keycloak vulnerable to information disclosure via CORS header injection due to unvalidated JWT azp claim
entry.content:
Keycloak vulnerable to information disclosure via CORS header injection due to unvalidated JWT azp claim

Aliases: CVE-2026-37977

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.4.13
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.6.3

A flaw was found in Keycloak. A remote attacker can exploit a Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) header injection vulnerability in Keycloak's User-Managed Access (UMA) token endpoint. This flaw occurs because the `azp` claim from a client-supplied JSON Web Token (JWT) is used to set the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header before the JWT signature is validated. When a specially crafted JWT with an attacker-controlled `azp` value is processed, this value is reflected as the CORS origin, even if the grant is later rejected. This can lead to the exposure of low-sensitivity information from authorization server error responses, weakening origin isolation, but only when a target client is misconfigured with `webOrigins: ["*"]`.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-v3pr-hxpr-mfm8: Apache MINA: Critical Deserialization Allow-list Bypass via resolveProxyClass
entry.content:
Apache MINA: Critical Deserialization Allow-list Bypass via resolveProxyClass

Aliases: CVE-2026-47065

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

  • org.apache.mina:mina-core — fixed in 2.0.29
